answers.answer:
Route table from the code at e02167f:
(1) 'gpt-live', live capture: `prepareSession` is an `aiAction`, which calls `requireUserId`, so only a signed-in user can start it. The server holds OPENAI_API_KEY and mints a client secret that lasts 60 s. The browser then POSTs its SDP offer to https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls with that secret, and the audio goes straight to OpenAI over WebRTC. It is authenticated but does not pass through our server.
(2) 'gpt-live', recovery of a kept recording: the recording is uploaded to the authenticated `transcribeAudio` action, which sends it to whisper-1 at https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions from the server.
(3) 'whisper', or no row (`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPTION = "whisper"`): `prepareSession` returns batch mode, and audio is uploaded through Convex to whisper-1 from the server.
(4) 'voxtral', 'transcribe', 'transcribe-medical': `transcriptionRoute` throws in its default branch, both in `prepareSession` and in `transcribeAudio`. These values are refused and nothing falls back to OpenAI.
(5) On-device test marker: `settings.update` calls `assertTestFixtureUser` when the value is "on-device-test", and that check only accepts an email ending in @roundai.test. `resolveDictationEngine` returns "cloud" for every other saved value. The native plugin is only reachable for engine "web-speech", which only the marker can produce, so a real account never reaches browser or native speech.
The question's pass rule would count row 1's short-lived server-minted secret as a pass. The oracle wins, and it judges row 1 (direct but authenticated) per Q2. That is the only point against the rule, so the verdict is pending:Q2. BAA coverage of each endpoint (S08), the production transcription value (S19) and the unit test results (static lane) belong to other halves.

How each route works at e02167f:

(1) 'gpt-live' live capture. transcribe.prepareSession is an aiAction, so it requires a signed-in user (requireUserId). On the server it mints an OpenAI realtime client secret that lasts 60 s. The project key stays on the server. The browser then posts its SDP offer straight to https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls using that short-lived secret, and the audio goes over WebRTC directly to OpenAI. So this route is authenticated but does not pass through our server.

(2) 'gpt-live' recovery of a kept recording, and (3) 'whisper' or no value. Both use transcribeAudio, which is also a signed-in aiAction. The audio is uploaded to Convex, which posts it to api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions with whisper-1. If no value is set, the default is DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPTION = "whisper".

(4) 'voxtral', 'transcribe' and 'transcribe-medical'. transcriptionRoute throws for these, and it runs before the OpenAI key is read. Nothing falls back to OpenAI.

(5) The on-device test marker. settings.update calls assertTestFixtureUser only when the value is "on-device-test", and that check refuses any email not ending in @roundai.test. resolveDictationEngine returns "cloud" for every other saved value. The native speech plugin is only selected when the engine is "web-speech", which only that marker can produce. So a real account can never reach Web Speech or the native recognizer.

Verdict: every point the code decides passes. The one point against the rule is row 1, which is direct from the browser to OpenAI but authenticated. The oracle hands that row to Q2, so the verdict is pending:Q2. Two other halves are not decided here: BAA coverage of each endpoint (S08) and which value production actually uses (S19). The unit tests are green in the static lane (context only).
